Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Jonathan Van Lange and Adnaan Lagadien open up for South Africa Under-19. Jakeem Pollard has the new ball in hand. Lets go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

When Zachary Carter and Jonathan Van Lange were out in the middle, 300 looked a real possibility, but West Indies have fallen well short of what they would have had in mind. Still, 234 is a competitive total on a wicket that has been slightly two-paced, with some balls skidding through, very few holding up, and the odd one keeping low. Whether it slows down with the sun beating down remains to be seen. Remember, two crucial points are at stake here. Whichever team wins this clash will carry points forward into the Super Six stage, while the loser will not take any points through. Back in a bit for the chase.

The star with the ball for South Africa, JJ Basson, is in for a chat. He says that they are happy with how they pulled things back and he is proud of the boys. Adds that he thought short ball was the best plan, spoke to the captain about it and is happy that he could execute it. Mentions that the 12th men and substitute fielders did a great job in keeping the energy of the boys to battle the heat. Ends by saying that their batters have been in form lately, and he is confident they will chase this down.

Tredness crept in under energy-sapping conditions, and Carter eventually perished. At that stage, Windies needed Van Lange to dig in, but he threw his wicket away soon after. Once he fell, the tail failed to muster much resistance, as the Proteas boys completed the clean-up job. JJ Basson was undoubtedly the pick of the bowlers, finishing with a five-wicket haul, while during the middle phase, Paul James and Michael Kruiskamp brought some much-needed control for South Africa.

Zachary Carter looked uncomfortable initially but grew in confidence and began taking on the change bowlers. Skipper Joshua Dorne walked in ahead of Jewel Andrew at number 3 and struggled to get his innings moving. Against the run of play, three wickets in a single over from JJ Basson reduced West Indies to 115/4. Carter then joined hands with Jonathan Van Lange to pull the innings back on track, with Carter going on to notch up his maiden Youth ODI hundred.

An innings that promised a lot, but it all fizzled out. From being 193/4, West Indies lost 6 wickets for 41 runs to be bowled out for 234. A job well done by South Africa, who showed great composure and skill in pulling things back after being put under pressure. After opting to bat first, it was a tough interrogation early on for the two Windies' openers, with the South African new-ball attack testing them with pace and some well-directed short balls.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! An eventful last few overs of the game. It all started with that triple strike from JJ Basson. Commentary.Commentary: The ball has been lost, and as the umpires pick the replacement, they have called for DRINKS. West Indies will be pretty happy with this start. It was tough early on as the South African new-ball attack bowled with serious pace, but they managed to see off that phase without much damage. Zachary Carter has settled in nicely and will look to convert this start into a big score. In these energy-sapping conditions, an arduous challenge awaits Muhammad Bulbulia and his boys. Whatever early assistance there was for the quicks has largely disappeared. Just three balls of spin have been bowled so far, and it remains to be seen how much, if anything, the spinners can extract from this dry surface. The ball that was dispatched out of the park has been found, and we carry on with it after the break.

PITCH REPORT - Ian Bishop shares that it is pretty warm out there, with not much wind to offer relief, and that could make it a tough outing for the players over the course of the match. Jon Kent joins him, and he describes it as a really good wicket. Informs that South Africa played Afghanistan here previously, and Corne Botha was able to extract pace and bounce, which highlights the true nature of the surface. Jon mentions that the pitch has a good grass covering and, according to him, it is the most impressive strip compared to the other wickets on the square. He observes that the grass has started to burn off, which could see the surface play slightly on the slower side.

The captain of South Africa Under-19, Muhammad Bulbulia says that they would have bowled first anyway. Adds that they want to strike early and make inroads as they have been doing in this tournament. Mentions that every game from now on is like a knock-out but they are not thinking about that much and will take it one game at a time.

The skipper of West Indies Under-19, Joshua Dorne feels that the surface looks like a good one and they want to put up a good total on the board. Calls it a really important game but stresses the need to play with freedom rather than added pressure. He adds that assessing the wicket early would be key before building the innings accordingly. Informs that they have one change with Isra-el Morton coming in for Matthew Miller.
